reviews.author: YennaPPa (Luscious.K)
reviews.text:
#Cheongdam-dong #Sushi Matsumoto



#Sushi King
There are two people in Korea who are called the Sushi Kings (in my personal opinion...),
These are Chef Morita of Shilla Hotel Ariake and Chef Matsumoto of Sushijo of Jeon Chosun Hotel.
The reason why these two chefs are called sushi kings is because they are the ones who laid the foundation for sushi in our country.
I think that the rapid development and upward standardization of sushi in our country was also due to the efforts of the students that chefs from Sushijo and Ariake have raised over the generations.

However, these two people left Korea around the same time and their fans were very disappointed, but they came back to Korea around the same time.
Chef Matsumoto is...
Chef Morita is an advisor to...

Since it was extremely difficult to make a reservation for both of them, I didn't bother to try, but after a vicious reservation war, I decided to come half way for my birthday.
Looking forward to experiencing the pinnacle of Korean sushi...

#Atmosphere #Service
It's a 9-seat Tachi sushi restaurant with an ordinary atmosphere, but the service is perfectly comfortable. He checks for my shortcomings in many ways and takes care of them without any shortcomings.
Even though we don't have perfect rapport with Chef Matsumoto, who speaks Korean reasonably well, we can have a pleasant conversation, and the sous chef provides detailed interpretation.
On the day I visited, Chef Nam Seong-hoon helped me comfortably.

#taste
Intense.
Honestly, it's the most intense sushi I've ever had.
It lacks the sweetness and focuses on the salty and sour flavors, but there may be some likes and dislikes about this.
If you eat shari alone, it seems like there is no balance between sweet and salty, but when combined with neta, the harmony increases to an incredible level of taste, and you can see that it is not simply salty, but was planned for a harmony of tastes.

Netas and Tsumami are all of a high standard. We tried to maximize the texture and taste of all ingredients, and of course, the harmony was excellent.
It's an explosion of flavor and continuous deliciousness from start to finish. Plus, the best suimono are amazing.#Unfamiliar taste of familiar ingredients
While eating over 20 different pieces, there is not a single new ingredient. However, the taste is different from the tastes I have had so far. I guess this is Matsumoto’s style.
- Jjawanmushi: It seems simple, but I really like it without the truffle oil scent that is common these days.
- Steamed abalone: ​​The perfect combination of chewy and soft. The most delicious crab sauce so far
- Hirame, Ankimo: A skill that allows you to fully enjoy the taste of the ingredients.
- Tacos, cockles, northern clams: A technique that exquisitely adjusts the boundary between freshness and fishy taste, leaving only the umami flavor.
- Snow crab meat and jelly ponzu: There’s no way crab meat prepared by someone else can’t taste good.. It’s sweet.
- Fries: The quality of the fries is slightly disappointing.
- Patterned squid + uni: If sushi restaurants have tofu rolls, Matsumoto has squid uni rolls. The one-handed pottery technique is unrivaled.
- Grilled gold tae: Matsumoto’s unique grilled gold tae that emphasizes softness. Excellent grilled geumtae that doesn't stand out as much as "uni bibim shari"
- Shima Aji: A perfect combination of strong shari and siromi + a delicious savory texture, the Shima Aji of your life
- Sea bream suimono: Mouthwatering with a clear and rich soup that seems to bring out the deep flavor of the sea bream.
- Herring: Nissing, one of the best sushi in Matsumoto. The best herring that has no fishy taste and is extremely refreshing.
- Madai: The sogginess of sea bream belly marinated in kelp.
- Gizzard shad: It's a pickled shad with a surprising salty taste, but I don't hate it. The best combination with sweet Dotssy.
- Akami: Honmaguro from Spain with a comforting taste without any strings, leaving only the savory and umami flavor.
- Judoro: The true taste of Judoro, with changes in fat content like deer hair
- Odoro: The salty taste calms the greasiness... It's a strange logic, but it's an amazing Odoro that you will agree with when you taste it.
- Miso soup: Life-long miso soup filled with the freshness of clam base
- Amaebi: Average
- Shime Saba: Shime is great, but the taste of slightly blown fire upgrades the taste.
- Yaki Negitoro: Seaweed made by grilling Odoro and finely chopping the white part of the green onion. This too is a negito of life
- Anago: I have never eaten anago this soft. make me laugh
- Gyoku: Korea’s highest level of gyoku. Silkyness and tanginess are the best
- Encore - Kappa Maki: This is an encore, but please do Kappa Maki instead of an encore. He gladly gave it to me, and the intensity of the shiso and ume showered my tongue at the end.
- Dessert: Monaca Sand, Matcha Ice Cream, Lemon Ice Cream. Maintain an ordinary but unique character

#likes and dislikes
This is a sushi restaurant that technically cannot be argued against.
Instead, there may be likes and dislikes regarding the style of taste.
It is the most intense sushi I have ever tasted, but it may be disappointing for those who like sweet tastes as the intensity is centered around salty and sour flavors.
However, the effort put into creating that taste is very visible.

All salt used in this house is made by roasting and hand-grinding the best domestic sea salt. It is the best salt with a combination of saltiness and complex sweetness. To be honest, I thought it was the highest quality foreign salt.
Gari is also made in-house, and compared to commercially available gari, it is less sweet and emphasizes sourness in a style that makes your mouth water.

It is impossible to argue whether one likes or dislikes Matsumoto-style sushi, which was created through technology and effort to support it.
If it's good, I think you just have to enjoy it.



PS: It's a very difficult place to make a reservation, but while making a reservation for this house, I found out that my iPhone can only store up to 200 recent call lists haha.

PS2: It was fun to actually see the one-hand squid potting technique, a feature of the Matsumoto family. (Photo 28)

PS3: House sake Matsumoto is very tasty for the price. It goes well with the strong taste of sushi here.

#Cheongdam-dong #Urang

“Cheongdam-dong’s neighborhood bar with a secret skill”

In the past, the most famous place in Cheongdam-dong was a place called Juliana.
It was in the basement of the Ellui Hotel, but when the hotel suddenly disappeared one day and was replaced with the most expensive apartment complex in Korea, the area lost its feel of an entertainment district and became a residential area.

However, I didn't even know that there was an izakaya in this neighborhood.
It's a strange location, but it's quite popular and has a lot of customers.
Of course, most of them are office workers around me.

It feels more like a local Korean pub than an authentic izakaya run by a Japanese chef.
Just in case, I asked about ‘potato salad’ and the owner looked puzzled.
'What is this?' It feels a bit like this haha
Anyway, this confirms it as a Korean-style tavern.

I ordered sashimi and it came out quite nice.
White fish is well aged and tastes good even if it has been cooked with konbujime.
Instead, Maguro is quite disappointing.

Besides the sashimi, which doesn't stand out too much, the real secret of this restaurant is the nabe dishes.
I have seen somewhere that food is boiled in paper nabe, but this restaurant places the paper nabe in a bamboo-like basket and uses it as cooking ware.
Urang Nabe is a non-spicy seafood nabe, and the sight is heart-stopping because it is filled with various seafood.
Instead, because there are too many bean sprouts, the first taste is that the bean sprout taste is dominant, which is unfortunate, but the more it boils, the more the broth tastes, and it becomes a pretty nice soup.
On the other hand, the more you boil it, the tougher the seafood becomes, so the point of eating it is to adjust it to your taste.
I choose the soup haha

It would be difficult to give an accurate evaluation in one visit, but I found a local izakaya that would be good to go and have another drink sometime.

reviews.author: ethan ghymn
reviews.text:
When I got home, I had to eat dinner outside of class, so there was traffic, and suddenly I couldn't go far. The hoisin rice bowl I had at The Round Samsung branch, which I stopped by last time, was good, so I was wondering if The Round Cheongdam main branch near my house would be better, so I decided to stop by.

I made a quick phone call and asked if there was any room at the bar counter. I was told there was, so I left right away.

I quickly arrived in front of the store and when I entered the store, it looked like it had been remodeled from a home, but it was a little more compact than the Samsang branch and had a cozy feel to put it nicely. They gave me directions to the bar counter, but the atmosphere was a bit worse than the bar counter at the Samsung branch, so I asked if there were any table seats, and they asked me if a table for two in the hallway would be okay. I said I would sit there, and I accepted the offer and sat down.

First, they brought me the menu and set the chamomile tea on the warmer. Since the menu was already decided, I asked for hoisin rice bowl without anything to look at, which I already knew, but when I inquired again if it was the same store as the Samsung branch, they said that this was the main branch in Cheongdam, perhaps because they were proud of the main branch. I had two good experiences at the SMT China Room Mondrian Hotel branch before, so the SMT House China Room Cheongdam branch, which is close to my house, also felt like the main branch, so I leaned on it. I remember being relatively disappointed when I stopped by, so I waited with half anticipation and half anxiety.

Just like in the Samsung branch, I could see the oven for roasting Peking duck, and on the way to the bathroom, I saw the second floor, so I went up and saw that the second floor consisted only of rooms.

The pickled radish that was set first was as expected sweet and sour, and the chai had a nice umami flavor.

After waiting a little longer, the hoisin rice bowl finally came out with a slightly more luxurious egg soup. It felt similar to the high-quality one, but it was a little different from the Samsung branch, with a more reddish tint. It contained a piece of abalone, scallops, and shrimp, but there was no sea cucumber. Aside from the abalone, it felt like the ingredients were more sparing than the Samsung branch, so it already felt like a failure.

First, when I tasted the egg soup, the one at the Samsung branch had a simple appearance but tasted more like a Chinese restaurant, whereas the one at the Cheongdam main branch had a somewhat Japanese feel, so although it looked good, it didn't taste any better.

This time, when I tasted the hoisin rice bowl, I liked the scent of bamboo shoots and ginger, and it tasted luxurious as expected, but I felt a little more of the subtle spiciness of the red pepper oil, which is expected from the red color. As expected, I felt it was a shame that they saved on the seafood, which is more expensive than the Samsung branch, and focused on squid.

However, the quality of the squid is good and soft, and the rice at the Samsung branch is sticky, so it's a type that seems to go better with the Korean menu, but the Cheongdam main branch has a fluffier type of rice, so it feels like it goes better with the Chinese menu.

The ingredients were a bit sparing and the spiciness was emphasized, but it didn't mean it wasn't delicious, so I ate it in moderation and tried to get up, but similar to the Samsung branch, they gave me mango simiro instead of mango sorbet as dessert, so I finished the meal neatly and got up.

Overall, I had a good experience at the SMT China Room Mondrian Hotel branch before, so I stopped by with the expectation that the SMT House China Room Cheongdam branch, which had the feel of the main branch but was closer to my house, would be better. I had an experience of feeling like a failure, so I stopped by here at The Round, hoping that it would not be a similar experience, but this time too, I felt like a failure. It cost about 18,000 won instead of 24,000 won, so I decided it was okay.

I don't know if it's just the hoisin rice bowl, but I think I'll go to the Samsung branch rather than the main branch in Cheongdam from now on.

I've always wanted to go to Jinju Hoegwan in Jung-gu or Jinju House in Yeouido, which are great bean noodle restaurants, but I still haven't been able to go there. Recently, I found out about Garam through Luscious.K's review. It's close to my house, and the menu is soybean noodle soup, and the noodles are not the common type, but the noodles I like are flat and soft, so I thought I'd stop by. But they're open on Sundays, so I called in advance to inquire about business hours, and they open at 3 o'clock. Break time is until 5 o'clock, but I was told that I could come by 2:30, so I left the house.

I quickly arrived in front of the store, and the brick exterior of the store reminded me of the house I grew up in, so it felt familiar. As I entered the store, there were tables in the center space, but in the main space, it seemed like I had to take off my shoes on the left and right sides and sit on the floor. In reality, it was a space where I had to put on my shoes, go up, and sit at the table. It was comfortable to go in with my shoes on, but I felt a little uncomfortable.

I sat down at the table and asked for the bean noodle soup that I had already decided on. They set out side dishes for me, but there were a lot of them and the volume was good, so I was a bit burdened because I don't like to leave anything behind.

After tasting all the side dishes one by one, it wasn't bad, but the kimchi was the best among them. However, the temperature wasn't cool and felt like room temperature, so it was a bit disappointing, and maybe not, but it wouldn't be a good idea to recycle the side dishes.

After waiting a bit, the bean noodles came out, and when I looked at them, I looked at them and they were of just the right amount, with sliced ​​cucumbers and half a hard-boiled egg as garnishes.

First, when I tasted the soybean soup, I felt a moderate savory taste. I usually don't season soybean noodles with salt, but this one also had a moderate savory taste and didn't seem to need any salt, so I started eating it.

As expected, the noodles are similar to Myeongdong Gyoza's kalguksu (noodles). They are flat, thin, and soft, so I don't know if they are a good match for the thick noodles of the type used in common bean noodles, but I like that type of noodles, so I like them.

It didn't contain a lot of noodles, so I quickly finished the noodles and drank a little soybean broth. Following Luscious.K's tip, I asked for sugar. After scooping the bean broth on a spoon and sprinkling some sugar on it, I tasted it and it was okay. I tasted it like that one more time, then added about two spoons generously with a teaspoon, stirred it around, and drank the bean broth. It felt like a slightly sweet misut powder with sugar, so I liked it. There's no need to drink anything like Gagel Naga coffee. It feels like killing two birds with one stone.

While calculating, do you think there are peanuts in the bean noodles? When I asked, I was told that sesame salt made from roasted sesame seeds was used, so I guess that was the secret to the proper flavor.

Overall, I like Kongguksu after seeing it in Luscious.K's review. I heard that it is a type of kalguksu noodles with flat, thin and soft noodles, so I stopped by because it seemed unusual. I'm not sure if it would immediately come to mind when I think of a Kongguksu restaurant, but I thought it was worth stopping by at least once when I was nearby and it was delicious.

This is a place where you can see a businessman trying to fool you.
After eating, many people only check the total amount and do not check the details, so take a close look at the details.

There was a new Chinese restaurant in the neighborhood, so I tried it out and there was a discount sign on the street, so I went in.
Of course, I ordered discounted items through the table kiosk.
However, when I went to the counter to pay after the meal, they asked for the non-discounted price.
So I asked if there was a discount event, and they said I should have gone to the kiosk's daily menu and placed an order.
So they said I had to pay the non-discounted price.
I felt bad

There was no sign at the door or kiosk indicating that discounted items must be ordered from the daily menu, and it would be common sense to assume that the prices would be the same regardless of whether they were on the daily menu or the regular menu. So does the discounted item only contain half the ingredients? Then you shouldn't even say discount, it's a scam.

I think it's not a matter of a few thousand won, but a matter of the attitude of the employees and the mindset of the food business.
I went in thinking about holding a family event there in September, but I think I'll have to look elsewhere.

Tables, chairs, even walls and ceilings with obvious cement marks, and mismatched yellow lighting. The salad was great to whet the appetite.
The second dish included stem beans and two pieces of corn. I ate stem beans with vegetable flavor. The corn was crispy and the oil was dripping.
The third dish was pasta. It was really the worst. The noodles were thick like udon noodles, the taste was like eating a lump of flour, and the spices, not to mention the sauce, didn't go well with it. After filling my stomach with this kind of food, I felt sick and was very upset.
The young male server changed the dishes, but he told me to remove the cutlery on the dishes. Should the customer remove the dishes and change them? And it's right to ask, not give instructions.
The fourth dish was Conchili pasta. It had a nice basil scent and felt like creamy pasta, but it was dry.
The main dish was served as the fifth dish. Lamb was brought out, but it was overcooked and seriously dry. The server, a young man with a tattoo on his arm, continued to provide the worst service. He came to bring the main dish, starting from instructing us to put away the cutlery, but there was previous food on the table, so he floated half the main bowl in the air at the end of the table and left only half of it on the table. Half of the bowl was sticking out. Who brings food like this? Even in a comfortable home, you don't do this. You have to move the existing dishes to the side, make space, and serve food. reviews.author: YennaPPa (Luscious.K)
reviews.text:
#Cheongdam-dong #Pecorino

"Taste as rich as the name"
“A black chic trattoria that rivals other restaurants”

It was a trattoria that became quite famous as soon as it opened, and I remember that there were more likes and dislikes than expected.
Maybe that's why it was one of the places I really wanted to go when it opened, but now it's become a place where I can either go or not go.

The reason for the visit is simple.
While looking for a place where I could comfortably enjoy champagne during the day on the weekend, I visited Pecorino because it was nearby.
It was a coincidence, but I was happy to visit this place because I had been curious about it since it opened.

The restaurant should be decorated in a vintage-chic black color.
In Seoul, where the distinction between osteria, trattoria, and restaurant has already collapsed, it may be meaningless to call the restaurant Trattoria OOOO, but this is the full name of this restaurant.
Considering the fairly calm and dark interior for a trattoria, the servers' attire and speech, and the alcohol serving station located in the middle of the restaurant, the atmosphere is comparable to that of a restaurant.

Looking at the menu, it's a trattoria.
Among these, we ordered dishes that were good for drinking wine and that allowed us to feel the unique characteristics of this restaurant.

#prosciutto
I ordered a wine starter.
It was spread with arugula, topped with fresh cut prosciutto, and finished with olive oil.
The combination of prosciutto and arugula is perfect, but what's disappointing is that the arugula at the bottom is just plain arugula.
I think the satisfaction with this menu would have increased dramatically if they had done a little work, such as at least mixing it with EVOO or combining EVOO with lemon.
As an amateur chef, don't you know the pecorino that professional chefs make?

#puttanesca
One of the best pastas to drink with is puttanesca.
I am very satisfied with the puttanescara, which tastes quite different from the version I make.
It has a strong anchovy flavor and the tomatoes that support it are good.
In addition, the curly texture of reginette is amazing and goes well with a side dish.
Pecorino version of Puttanesca!
I am truly satisfied.

#Carbonara
Original Carbonara.
The name of the restaurant is Pecorino, so if they can't make this pasta, they have to close.
But they make it well.
The exact taste of lard and the taste of cheese go well together to create an amazing salty taste, so it goes well with white wine.

#premeal bread
I wish you would just give me the bread.
If you ask for more, you will be charged extra.
The bread is really delicious.
Instead, I would like to use olive oil, which has a slightly more fragrant oil.
The taste of bread is coated with oil.

Overall, it is a delicious restaurant.
The atmosphere is good and the response is good.
Aside from the fact that it's expensive because it's Cheongdam, the food is good, so it's natural to visit again.
Instead, I want you to remove what needs to be removed.

The fact that same-day reservations are possible even during peak hours means that things are going downhill.
It is a time when restaurants need to improve their constitution.

reviews.author: World Travelist
reviews.text:
Meal budget per person (excluding drinks)
Category 2 (less than KRW 120,000, USD 100)

Owner-chef Emilio Brosso serves Cheongdam-dong Italian cuisine named after himself.
His journey of taste includes authentic Italian cuisine and local flavors enjoyed in Korea.
It is said that even the Italian ambassador visits here when he misses the food of his hometown.
The restaurant boasts a nice atmosphere with a large, open terrace.

- Coze (24K), starting from Tagliere (39K), is a spicy mussel stew cooked in tomato sauce and is a great antipasto to enjoy with champagne or white wine.
- Paccheri Pasta (30K) is a flavorful pasta dish served with truffle sauce and Parmigiano cheese with poached eggs. The chewy texture of the Paccheri is great.
- Tagliata di Manzo (90K) is a Secondi, beef filet with arugula, Parmigiano and balsamic.
- Diavola Pizza (28K) is a good combination of mozzarella, salami, and peperoncino.
- Corkage is 50K per bottle.

It may seem more expensive than other Italian restaurants, but the taste is even better.
Especially the paccheri pasta is the best!

The staff are friendly and attentive.
This restaurant is especially recommended for couples, friends, and families. It is also recommended for those who want to experience and enjoy high-quality Italian cuisine.
Valet parking service is also provided to ensure a comfortable visit.

reviews.author: YennaPPa (Luscious.K)
reviews.text:
#Cheongdang-dong #Peulla

“Clash of kindness and taste”

I wonder how many places in Korea you can eat casual Italian food, including pizza and pasta.
Perla is an Italian restaurant positioned to meet those needs, and it had good reviews, so I visited with high expectations.

The atmosphere is calm and cozy.
The servers are also friendly and I am satisfied.
All requests are accepted.

However, there are some things about the food that leave something to be desired.

The pizza dough is pretty good, but it smells a bit like flour and is hard.
In the case of pizza using tomato sauce, the tomato sauce is too watery, so the dough cannot stand it and becomes soggy.
The same thing happened to Bismarck.

The melanzane was also watery due to the too thin tomato sauce.

The fried calamari is served with aioli instead of the standard tomato sauce. Rather than traditional Italian fried calamari, it was a bit disappointing because it felt more like a beer-infused beer, similar to that of an upscale snack bar.
Instead, it's delicious.

The most satisfying menu item was the truffle pasta.
The aroma of the black truffle added to the dish is natural, and the softness and viscosity of the sauce are also good.
The texture of raw noodles is also excellent.

Mezzimaniche made from bisque (small rigatoni) is too firm, beyond al dente.
I like it al dente, but I think cooking it a little longer will help it adhere better to the sauce.

You are abundant because you are generous.

This is not a soggy franchise-level lasagna.

A wonderful piece of fine dining quality.

#papiotte
Tongyeong red sea bream, cuttlefish, clam, shrimp, tomato, spinach, herbs

It makes you want to drink a soup full of the flavor of the ingredients.

#chocolate fondant
A fondant cake with melted rich dark chocolate.
The sincerity with which they serve you warmly is beautiful.
As expected from a chef who is particularly good at desserts, the seafood course is a beautiful ending and a strong one.

Elena Young may seem simple, but she has great taste.
Cho Yong-pil, who is called the King of Singer, had a former nickname of Little Giant, and Elena Young's food is exactly like that.

There are two sorbets for dessert, but the first sorbet is a very bright sorbet that has a cleansing feel and does not have the taste of a dessert you usually think of.
The second sorbet was a good dessert as it had yogurt chunks, peach flavored sorbet, and some peach pieces.

The kitchen was open, so I could hear everything being said, but as the course ended, the conversation got louder. It was a bit uncomfortable to eat while listening to things I didn't really want to hear, and it really ruined the quiet atmosphere.

#Cheongdam-dong #GTS Burger

“As expected, it’s delicious if you don’t have any expectations.”

I thought it was a red ocean saturated with handmade burger restaurants, but something keeps popping up.
GTS Burger is one of those places.
I was surprised that my son would order a burger here, and I was also curious about what burgers are like these days, so I ordered one of the basic burgers, the GTS Bacon Cheese Burger.

I really like the burger.
The packaging is pretty and doesn't look unreasonable.
Some burger places put the contents asymmetrically in a way that makes the packaging look pretty, making it difficult to eat in the end, but this restaurant has carefully stacked the contents in layers and the packaging is also tasteful.

The patty is smashed style. Just a delicious patty with no flaws. The meat flavor is also appropriate.
I like the brioche bun.
It's so soft that there's no dull, miserable feeling. It has the strength and softness to support the contents well until the end of eating.
There is no splashing sauce, which brings out the unique taste of the burger.
There are quite a few burgers covered in sauce, but it's better to be moderate rather than excessive.
However, a chronic problem with Korean burgers is the cookedness of the bacon... I think it would be better to cook it a little more crispy.

I ate it without thinking, but it tasted better than I expected, so I was very satisfied.
The number of menu items at this restaurant is huge, and I'm not sure if everything will be delicious, but I'm satisfied with the basic GTS Burger.

#GTS Burger
I looked up the brand and found that it was already launched in 2020 and is a fairly large franchise with over 20 stores.
They say they aim for high-quality burgers using 100% refrigerated beef.
The name GTS Burger, which comes from the slogan Great Taste, Superior Quality, is said to have the power of a GTS version of the car.
Perhaps the founder, CEO Hyeonjae Lee, is a person who really likes cars.

reviews.text:
This newly opened high-end restaurant is a luxurious private fine dining space run by owner and chef Lee Sang-cheol, who has extensive experience at Imperia Hotel in Japan.
All courses, from appetizers to desserts, are personally managed by Chef Lee Sang-cheol, who sometimes transforms into a chef who is passionate about cooking, and sometimes a friendly bartender who listens to the guests' stories.
It is a small space that can accommodate up to 6 people, providing a private and special experience just for you.

The Teppanyaki Sogo set costs 200,000 won for both lunch and dinner.

Comparing the prices with Tamayura, another restaurant I like, Tamayura is more competitive for lunch and here for dinner.

The kelp-ripened oysters and mussel soup served as appetizers are the start of a gastronomic journey with a unique, confident flavor and refreshing taste.

Teppanyaki scallops are a great way to finish off your white wine and move on to red wine.
The signature handmade hamburger steak was served before the main course, which was a bit unusual but really delicious in a very unique style.
Next comes the flavorful barley shrimp teppanyaki.
Salt-grilled abalone on an iron plate has a taste similar to Tamayura, with a chewy texture and savory flavor.
Now comes the main dish, lobster teppanyaki. Homemade ricotta cheese and bisque cream sauce make a fantastic combination.
1++ Chateaubriand Korean beef aged for 4 weeks is tender and juicy. (Grilled Korean beef + tenderloin chateaubriand)
The fried rice with abalone intestines is a bit salty for my taste, but it's always a smart choice to end a meal with fried rice to keep you feeling full.

I really enjoyed dining at this restaurant with my friends who are true foodies.
This restaurant is great for couples or friends, as well as business or family gatherings.
Valet parking service is also provided to ensure a comfortable visit.

I visited in mid-to-late October.

Strangely enough, I was satisfied with everything except the menus that appeared in Black and White Chef.

In the Jang Trio, I could barely taste any of the other sauces except for the red pepper paste. (The meat also feels a bit tough)

The flounder seaweed soup and the vongole pasta sauce were too salty.

I paid extra for lobster and ate it, but I chewed the lobster shell. Since I told you, it must have been delivered to the kitchen.

(There was no additional follow-up)

The dessert was delicious, but the xylitol candy was a bit hard on my teeth as I am now well over 40.

There were criticisms that the tables were too close together, but maybe because I lived in Paris, I didn't feel like they were that close (I don't have to worry about what's happening next to me...).

And the last drawback is that the men's room has a bit of a smell. It somehow seems like a problem with the building itself. Even though I used a lot of diffusers, there was a bit of a bad smell.

Now, the good thing is that I really liked the reinterpretation of Korean food, starting with amuse bouche.

The pasta itself was really delicious. Although the vongole was a bit salty, the pasta itself was excellent.

The desserts that came out at the end were all good (except for the xylitol candy). Above all, the sommelier who served our table was very kind. Thanks to this person, the disappointing taste and atmosphere were greatly offset.

For some reason, the day we visited was the day that actress Kim Soo-mi passed away, and Chef Choi went to pay his respects and was not in our time zone, so I personally think that the final courses may have been lacking something.

Since it has been difficult to make a reservation for a while, I think I will try to visit again later next year.

reviews.text:
I had lunch. There is no place to store your coats and there is no place to put your bags or luggage, so you have to place them on a chair, on the floor, or on the shelf behind you. There were two tall and handsome male servers. When new food was served, all the used dishes were removed at the same time. He held up the cleaned dishes and explained the food, but it looked uncomfortable and the used dishes were clearly visible, which made me feel uncomfortable. It was an open kitchen, and the people in the kitchen were all good-looking.
Truffle sugar was served as the first dish. The warm, slightly salty truffle cream with a thin choux shell was delicious.
The second dish was fish and chips. They wrapped aged flounder with white kimchi and perilla oil and placed it on top of potato chips. It tasted like dried seaweed. It had a wasabi flavor and the chewy flounder and crispy potato chips were good.
The third dish was Mexican tart. It was a Mexican-style barbecued pork belly tart topped with guacamole, and it had a slightly spicy curry-like finish. The tart was like a thin butter ring and the chewy pork belly was very chewy and whetted my appetite.
Egg noodles were served as the fourth dish. The sauce was made with ssamjang, and chives and parmesan cheese were sprinkled on the garlic pickles and Iberico rib meat. I liked the crunchy texture and sweet taste of the garlic pickle. The savory rib liver meat was well seasoned and chewy, and when eaten with egg noodles, it harmonized well and was delicious.
Pork belly was served as the fifth main course. Hangjeong pork belly was cooked at low temperature for 12 hours, and below, marinara, tare sauce, spicy sauce made from raw garlic, and finely chopped cabbage were stir-fried and placed next to it.  The dishes were warm so I was able to eat at a constant temperature, and the sauce had a strong mala flavor.
Sixth, chocolate, ice cream, and tea came out. The chewy chocolate flavor and gelato-like chewy ice cream were very delicious.
It's good for a one-time meal, but the system and service were disappointing. If I visit nearby, I don't think I'll come back again. Still, it was a delicious meal.

After enjoying a delicious hoisin rice bowl at The Round Samsung branch, I took a walk and looked around the neighborhood on the way home. It was near the Round Cheongdam branch and I wondered if it had a better atmosphere than the Samsung branch. But when I looked at it again today, it looked similar and didn't look any better. I wanted to walk a little further. As I was snooping around here and there, I noticed various stores like Pecorino and Sushi Ryosen that I had saved in I Want to Go, and I guess I hadn't seen them because I hadn't paid much attention to them.

I looked to see if there was another store I had saved in I Want to Go nearby, and saw Bing Bing Bing here. Before going to Onelan The Round Samsung branch, I was planning to stop by Anko, which had good red bean shaved ice, but when I looked at the menu outside the store, I saw that there was a single person menu as well, so I decided to stop by this place.

The weather wasn't warm yet and there were no customers in the store, probably because it was the weekend. As I entered the store, I was greeted by a relatively elegant female owner who was sitting inside the kitchen.

I think the representative menu item is probably milk shaved ice, but I like classic red bean shaved ice. When I asked how it differs from milk shaved ice, I was told that red bean shaved ice is a type of milk shaved ice with red beans.

He prepared the food in the kitchen and waited a little while to bring it to me. He told me that if you pour the red beans on top of the shaved ice, the milk shaved ice will melt quickly, so scoop up the red beans a little and eat it together.

First, when I tasted the milk shaved ice, I was familiar with the snow-like soft texture, but it felt softer and subtly sweet.

This time, I tasted it with the red beans that they prepared themselves, and it was still good, but it seemed like they paid attention to the soft texture. The overall quality of the red bean shaved ice was better than Hyeonbaek Miltop, Anko, which I tried to stop by earlier, or Banpo Sounbing, which was good value for money, but I don't feel like I want to come again.

It tends to melt quickly, so I ate it in moderation and enjoyed it quickly, then returned the tray and went out.

Overall, it's been a while since I saved this place in I Want to Go, but I happened to see it while taking a walk, so I stopped by. It was a type of shaved ice that paid attention to the soft texture of the milk shaved ice, and I didn't feel that it was better than the stores I mentioned earlier or that it was unique to this place, so I thought it was okay.

reviews.author: YJ Oh
reviews.text: A bakery cafe located in a quiet Cheongdam-dong residential area behind Yeongdong High School. This place was previously operated under the name ‘Rollinwood’. Because it is located on the first floor of a building built on a slope, it feels like a 1.5 floor. The store is not large, but the interior is well decorated to create a cozy atmosphere. When you enter the entrance, there is a main hall and ordering counter on the right, and a bar-style table and chairs are placed by the window on the left. The walls are filled with small, pretty candles of various shapes for use on cakes, making it fun to look at them. You can also purchase regular cakes, but unlike other bakery cafes, this store mainly sells custom-made luxury cakes, and the quality of the cakes is another level. It was my first time seeing a cake decorated with fresh orchids placed on top of it like a flower arrangement, but I was surprised twice by the high price as well as the beautiful design. A variety of pretty cupcakes are also displayed and sold. It is famous for its special cakes made to order, and is a pretty cafe with a sentimental and cutely decorated interior. Valet parking appears to be available.

If you look at the price, it seems expensive, but I think the Pava cake costs well over 30,000 won, so it's definitely not expensive!
